items.title: periodic heartbeat recovery 'escalated' outcome is terminal: issue silently abandoned, never retried, no notification
items.body:
## What happened

Issue `5c23ba28-37f3-4468-94b8-639d49f13380` (identifier `DIN-12`, agent `james-blue-knx-frontend-ux`) had its heartbeat run fail at 13:31:02 (upstream 400 from the model provider — unrelated Hermes-side bug, not the point here). One `periodic heartbeat recovery` sweep later picked it up:

```
13:47:02 WARN: periodic heartbeat recovery changed assigned issue state
{"promotedScheduledRetries":0,"promotedScheduledRetryRunIds":[],
 "assignmentDispatched":0,"dispatchRequeued":0,"continuationRequeued":0,
 "dispositionRepairRequeued":0,"productiveContinuationObserved":0,
 "successfulContinuationObserved":0,"orphanBlockersAssigned":0,
 "successfulRunHandoffEscalated":0,"reviewParticipantRequeued":0,
 "escalated":1,"waitingOnReviewResolved":0,"providerQuotaMonitored":0,
 "recentProgressExempted":0,"operatorCancelExempted":0,
 "onboardingFirstTaskExempted":0,"skipped":6,
 "issueIds":["5c23ba28-37f3-4468-94b8-639d49f13380"]}
```

That is the **last time this issue appears anywhere in the recovery sweep output** — every sweep since (running every ~60s) reports `"issueIds":[]`, i.e. it no longer considers this issue at all. No new run was dispatched (`assignmentDispatched: 0` on that same tick), no comment was posted to the issue, no interaction/notification was created (checked `POST .../interactions` and `POST .../comments` in the surrounding logs — none), and no board/operator-facing signal fired. The only traffic against the issue afterward is plain `GET` calls from someone loading the UI and noticing nothing is happening.

Net effect: **55+ minutes (and counting) of complete silence** on an issue that a human has to notice is stuck purely by looking at the board and realizing no run has occurred in a suspiciously long time. Nothing in the product told us.

## Why this matters

This is the same failure *shape* as several open issues already in this tracker, just a different trigger:

- #13532 — skipped handoff wake is terminal, no run, no retry
- #12883 — review-stage escalation strips the monitor, leaves the issue with no wake path
- #9201 — run-recovery parks issues in `blocked` and never wakes the recovery owner → permanent zombie
- #11112 — comment-wake silently skipped for stale `running` agents → permanently unwakeable
- #13419 — recovery backstop mislabels fast failures, drops the real error

Across all of these, some code path reaches a state it treats as "handled" (skipped / escalated / parked / cleared) without actually guaranteeing one of the three things a terminal outcome must guarantee: a scheduled retry, a real human-visible notification, or a timer to re-evaluate later. `escalated: 1` in the periodic-heartbeat-recovery counters reads as if the platform did something about it, but nothing observable happened.

## Suggested fix direction

Given how many independent trigger paths land in this same silent-terminal state, it's probably worth a single invariant enforced centrally rather than patching each trigger: whenever the recovery/escalation logic marks an issue as handled (`escalated`, `skipped`, parked in `blocked`, monitor cleared, etc.), it must synchronously do at least one of:
1. schedule a concrete retry/wake, or
2. create a real interaction/comment/notification a human will see, or
3. set a bounded re-check timer.

If none of those can be established, that itself should be a loud error, not a silently "successful" sweep result.

## Repro data

- Company: `826eb119-a439-490a-8dae-dad39f6ee5e2`, issue `DIN-12` (`5c23ba28-37f3-4468-94b8-639d49f13380`)
- `paperclipai` server log excerpt above, timestamps 13:31:02 (failure) → 13:47:02 (escalated, terminal) → now (60+ sweeps later, still `issueIds":[]`, zero dispatch)
- Related Hermes-side bug that triggered the original failure (thinking-block duplication on heartbeat continuation), filed separately: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123923

items.title: wake-queue reopen activity record names the releasing run, not the comment/run that asked to reopen
items.body:
## What happened?

When the wake-queue reopens a `done` issue after a deferred comment, the `issue.updated` activity record is written with the **releasing** run's id, not the run/comment that asked for the reopen. The record therefore reads as "the run that closed this issue reopened it," which looks like a lock or cron fault. In our deployment this mis-attribution cost several agent heartbeats of wrong diagnosis before the true trigger was found.

Observed on a real occurrence: triggering comment `7a42dd5c` at 10:32:07.232Z, deferred 28m 49.9s, drained at 11:00:57.139Z — 6m 19.5s after the 10:54:37.682Z close. The reopen activity record names run `308f4ddd` (the closing run) and not comment `7a42dd5c`.

## Expected behavior

The reopen activity record should carry the reason for the reopen: the requesting comment id(s), the requesting actor type/id, and the wake id. `runId` should remain the releasing run, but be distinguishable from the requester.

**The reopen itself is correct and must not change.** It is a deliberate feature, pinned by `services/issue-comment-wakeup.test.js` (`"does not wake a closed issue unless the comment reopened it"`, `"preserves explicit resume from a completed prior run"`). An explicit mention of the assignee on a closed issue must be answerable.

## Steps to reproduce (deterministic, no timing luck needed)

1. Create issue `X`, assign agent `A`.
2. Agent `A` starts a run on `X` so `X` is in flight and locked.
3. Agent `B` posts a comment on `X` mentioning `[@A]`. The mention wake cannot be delivered and is deferred to `deferred_issue_execution`.
4. Agent `A` closes `X` as `done` in that same run. The close clears all four lock columns (`services/issues.js:7081-7086`).
5. `A`'s run releases its queue. The drain finds the deferred mention, and because `status === "done"`, `candidate.agentId === assigneeAgentId`, `requestedByActorType === "agent"`, `deferredContextSeed.resumeIntent === true` and `queuedCommentIds.length > 0`, it reopens `X` to `todo` (`modules/wake-queue/application/use-cases.js:246-254`, then `reopenIssue` at `modules/wake-queue/adapters/postgres.js:301-304`).
6. Read `GET /api/issues/{X}/activity`. The reopen entry has `details.source = "deferred_comment_wake"`, `reopened: true`, `reopenedFrom: "done"` — and `runId` equal to **step 4's run**, i.e. the closing run.

## Suggested patch (3 changes, no behaviour change)

**1. Carry the reason on the effect.** `modules/wake-queue/application/use-cases.js:288-296`. `workingCandidate` is already in scope and already carries every field needed:

```js
postCommitEffects.push({
    kind: "issue_reopened",
    companyId: reopened.companyId,
    agentId: invokableAgent.id,
    runId: run.id,                       // the RELEASING run — ambiguous today
    requestedByAgentId: workingCandidate.requestedByActorId,
    requestedByActorType: workingCandidate.requestedByActorType,
    wakeId: workingCandidate.id,
    triggerCommentIds: workingCandidate.queuedCommentIds,
    issueId: reopened.id,
    identifier: reopened.identifier,
    reopenedFrom: currentIssue.status,
});
```

**2. Log it.** `services/heartbeat.js:6288-6294`. Copy the new fields into `details` and add `requestedByRunId` next to the existing `runId` so the two are never confusable again.

**3. Test.** Assert the reopen activity record names the requesting comment id and the requesting actor type, and that `runId` is documented as the releasing run.

## Two adjacent observations (same area, optional)

- **`executionLockedAt` is stamped at promotion, not checkout.** `modules/wake-queue/adapters/postgres.js:352-360` writes `executionLockedAt: input.now` when the wake is promoted; `issue.checked_out` is logged when the run actually starts. Measured skew in our occurrence: **304.1s**. Staleness is decided by run *status*, not lock age (`isCleanable`, `services/recovery/service.js:4111-4118`), so this is not a correctness bug — it is a measurement trap for anyone reasoning about lock age. Either set the column at checkout or add a separate `promotedAt`.
- **A lock-only sweep mutates `updatedAt`.** `services/recovery/service.js:4131` sets `updatedAt: new Date()` while clearing lock columns, so a `done` issue's `updatedAt` advances with no agent write. That makes `updatedAt` unusable as a "last real change" signal. Suggest not bumping `updatedAt` on lock-only writes, or logging the bump distinctly.

## Investigated and NOT defects (so nobody re-files)

- `issue.stale_lock_cleared` **cannot** de-terminal an issue. `services/recovery/service.js:4124-4139` sets only the four lock columns plus `updatedAt`; `status` is absent. The only status write in that sweep is to `heartbeatRuns.status`, not the issue.
- A `done` transition **already** clears every lock column in the same write. `services/issues.js:7081-7086`.

## What we are asking for

A version that carries the reopen reason in the activity record. No behaviour change requested, no migration, no config. Happy to re-run the repro above against a fix release and confirm the activity record names the requesting comment.

## Environment

- Paperclip version: `2026.916.1`
- Deployment mode: Self-hosted server (local trusted, private exposure)
- Database: External Postgres
- Adapters involved: core bug — not adapter-specific (Hermes agents, but the mis-attribution is server-side)
- Access context: Agent (bearer API key)
- OS: macOS 26 (Apple Silicon)

items.title: Flaky: runnerd-codex-transport lost-ack test races the commit-drain window (blocks PR #14076)
items.body:
Opened while triaging https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14076 (KEE-956). This is a master-side flake, independent of that PR.

## The failing test

```
src/live/runnerd-codex-transport.test.ts > preserves old warm-attach authority and event ownership across lost-ack
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'logicalEffectCount')
  at src/live/runnerd-codex-transport.test.ts:4473:30
```

Shard 1/2 of `Verify Paperclip Runner (vitest 1/2)`, on a run where the other 996 tests in the lane passed.

## Why it is a race, not a logic break

The test captures a held event only when `armed && mode !== 'rejected-attach' && heldEvent === null && event.eventType === 'run.attached'` (line 4299-4302). In `mode === 'lost-ack'` it calls `core.disconnectActiveRunner()` (line 4465), releases the blocked commit, and then requires the warm attach to re-commit that held event.

The assertion at 4471-4473 is:

```ts
const attachedEvent = retired.committedEvents.find(
  (entry) => entry.sourceEventId === heldEvent!.sourceEventId,
)!;
expect(attachedEvent.logicalEffectCount).toBe(1);
```

`retired.committedEvents.find(...)` can return `undefined` when the held `run.attached` event has not drained into the retired set yet. The non-null assertion suppresses the type error, so the next property read throws a `TypeError` that does not name the real cause.

The window being raced is commit-drain across a forced disconnect. Nothing about the assertion is wrong; it is unguarded against timing.

## Suggested fix directions

1. Wait for the condition instead of assuming it. The file already has a `within(label, promise, ms)` helper used throughout, so the same pattern would fit here.
2. Or assert the precondition explicitly so a genuine regression reports as a clear failure rather than a `TypeError`.

## Evidence it is not specific to one PR

- `runnerd-codex-transport.test.ts` is byte-identical between `origin/master` and the head of #14076, and that PR changes zero files under `packages/paperclip-runner`.
- On this host the file fails on pristine `origin/master` too, with a *different* test failing across runs, which is the signature of load sensitivity rather than a deterministic defect.
- `e006c18f2` ("test(paperclip-runner): stabilize the assigned-skills ACPX runtime host test`, merged 2026-09-24) shows this lane has needed stabilising before.

Filing from the Keece DevOps Automator seat. Not a Keece product defect; the Keece change in #14076 is server-side only.

items.title: Implicit reopen guard on comment repost (DELETE+POST) not extended to authorAgentId: null (user-authored) path
items.body:
## Description

Reported upstream by a Paperclip company (RaciFlow, RAC-13549). A `DELETE` + `POST` on an issue comment (the only edit path available — no `PATCH`/`PUT`, confirmed by an `OPTIONS` probe) triggers `issue_reopened_via_comment` even when the issue is `done` and the repost has no substantive change (a typo fix only).

Measured: 3 close→reopen cycles in 37 minutes on the same issue, several agent heartbeats burned for nothing.

## Context

The implicit reopen guard already exists for agent-authored comments (`resume:true`, related to the guard discussed in #3980 / `shouldImplicitlyReopenCommentForAgent`). It is not applied to the author-user path (`authorAgentId: null`) — i.e. when a human (or an agent acting as a board user, delete+repost being the only correction mechanism) reposts a comment with no meaningful content change, the issue still gets kicked from `done` back to an active status.

This is distinct from:
- #3980 (closed) — agent comment misattributed to `local-board`, causing the guard to miss self-comments.
- #3433 (closed) — comment wakes firing on `blocked`/`done`/`cancelled` regardless of authorship, unrelated to the reopen guard itself.

## Suggested fix

Extend the existing `resume:true` implicit-reopen guard to also cover `authorAgentId: null` (user-authored) comment reposts when there's no meaningful content change — same guard, wider actor coverage, not a new mechanism.

## Reporter's workaround (already applied, out of scope here)

The reporting company's own skill (`issues-blocked`) no longer auto-corrects a mojibake via delete+repost, to avoid re-triggering this. This issue is only about the upstream guard gap.

items.title: Auth rate limiting falls back to one shared bucket behind a reverse proxy (no way to set Better Auth's client IP header)
items.body:
### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I am on the latest released version of Paperclip (or can reproduce on `master`).
- [x] I have confirmed the error originates in Paperclip itself (not in my agent adapter, API provider, or local configuration).

### What happened?

On an authenticated + public instance behind a reverse proxy, the server logs this on requests to the auth routes:

```
WARN [Better Auth]: Rate limiting could not determine a client IP and is falling back to a single shared per-path bucket. Ensure your runtime forwards a trusted client IP header, then set `advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders`
```

The proxy does forward the client address (Railway's edge sets both `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP`), but Paperclip has no setting that reaches Better Auth's `advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders`. In `server/src/auth/better-auth.ts`, `buildBetterAuthAdvancedOptions` only sets `cookiePrefix` and `useSecureCookies`. `TRUST_PROXY` configures Express, but Better Auth reads the headers itself, so it doesn't help here.

With one shared bucket per path, anyone who can reach the sign-in page can use up the limit for every user of the instance, and the limit no longer slows down a single client.

### Expected behavior

A way to tell Better Auth which header carries the client IP, for example an env var such as `PAPERCLIP_AUTH_IP_HEADERS=x-real-ip` passed through as `advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders`, or deriving it from the existing `TRUST_PROXY` setting. It should stay opt-in, since trusting a header the proxy doesn't overwrite would let clients pick their own IP.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `ghcr.io/paperclipai/paperclip:latest` with `PAPERCLIP_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=authenticated`, `PAPERCLIP_DEPLOYMENT_EXPOSURE=public` and `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` set, behind any reverse proxy that sets `X-Forwarded-For` (I used Railway).
2. Call `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email` a few times.
3. The warning above appears in the server log.

### Paperclip version or commit

v2026.916.1, commit d554c4789ed3930f8a53ac9fdf6503b3187097da (from `/api/health`).

### Deployment mode

authenticated / public

### Installation method

Docker image

### Additional context

I found this while building and testing a Railway template for Paperclip (I publish Railway templates and Railway pays template authors a share of hosting usage). Happy to open a PR if you tell me which shape you prefer: a new env var, or reuse `TRUST_PROXY`.
